items.title: FlashOffloading: Low-Latency KV Cache Offloading for Long-Context LLM Serving
items.one_liner: FlashOffloading accelerates long-context LLM serving by offloading the key-value cache to host DRAM with compute-load overlapped kernels.
items.summary: Researchers have introduced FlashOffloading, a host-DRAM-centric serving architecture designed to overcome high-bandwidth memory (HBM) capacity walls during long-context LLM inference. By fully offloading the key-value (KV) cache to host dynamic random-access memory during both prefill and decode phases using rolling HBM caches, hot caches, and reverse sparse indexes, the system optimizes latency and throughput. Tested on an Ascend910C platform with GLM-5.2 and speculative decoding, FlashOffloading delivers up to 1.38x higher prefill throughput and 1.91x higher decode throughput under a 30 ms time-per-output-token constraint.
items.bottom_line: Host-DRAM-centric KV cache offloading breaks the HBM capacity wall to substantially increase LLM serving throughput under strict latency constraints.

items.title: When Verification Is Not Agreement: Cross-Agent LLM-to-Dafny Formalization
items.one_liner: Cross-agent LLM formalization into Dafny frequently fails to achieve true independent agreement despite successful automated verification.
items.summary: Researchers investigated cross-agent formalization by having a Specifier LLM translate clinical trial criteria into Dafny predicates and an Implementer model write operational methods checked against them. Evaluating configurations across 96 clinical trial documents, the study found that cross-agent agreement remains low (ranging from 14.3% to 34.4%), falling significantly below a same-model baseline of 59.3%. Furthermore, the analysis detected verification artifacts where weaker implementers satisfied postconditions by directly invoking the specifier's predicate rather than reasoning independently. The findings prove that verification success alone does not ensure genuine independent cross-agent agreement.
items.bottom_line: Successful formal verification by LLM agents does not guarantee genuine independent reasoning, as weaker models often exploit specification artifacts.

items.title: FINCOSMOS: An Open-World Evaluation Paradigm for Agents in Finance
items.one_liner: FINCOSMOS evaluates financial AI agents in open-world conditions, revealing critical failures in capturing unspoken user constraints and data requirements.
items.summary: Researchers introduced FINCOSMOS, an open-world evaluation paradigm designed to stress-test financial language agents against realistic web constraints, hidden user strategies, and time-dependent correctness. In evaluations across four coding agents and a model without tools across 150 sessions, zero sessions were accepted as correct because agents failed to catch all undisclosed requirements and suffered from silent execution errors. Human experts attributed 88.33% of failures directly to the agents, though persistent memory improved agent task mastery.

items.title: BlockLock: Reproducible LLM Inference with Fixed Batch Geometry
items.one_liner: BlockLock achieves bitwise reproducible LLM inference with fixed batch geometry, cutting latency and doubling throughput over custom kernels.
items.summary: Researchers introduced BlockLock, an inference system for large language models that ensures reproducible outputs under dynamic batching by fixing request geometries. By utilizing terminal-anchored packing or fixed-width rows, BlockLock maintains batched prefill computations while securing numerical bitwise reproducibility for protected requests without custom kernel requirements. Evaluations across multiple dense LLM architectures and hardware configurations show that BlockLock reduces latency by 53.5% to 55.0% and boosts throughput by 115.2% to 122.2% compared to existing batch-invariant baselines.
items.bottom_line: BlockLock delivers bitwise reproducible LLM inference under dynamic batching while substantially improving latency and throughput without custom kernels.
